title: Require producer to run full cargo test --locked; return not-run
summary: Replace line 8 of the producer frame prompt with a must-run rule for `cargo test --locked` on every change, including docs, TOML and data-only ones. Add a gate in the job flow: if the producer's report shows that test run as `not-run`, re-invoke the producer once rather than passing the candidate to verification. Audience: the Athena maintainer, who judges whether docs-only candidates stop reaching verification with an unrun test suite.

defaults_applied.how: The new gate gets a test, and cargo test and clippy must stay clean.
The prompt rule and the gate that enforces it are both changed, so the rule is not left as an unenforced request.
The not-run rule is enforced in the job flow, not only stated in prose.
One retry, no new config keys, and no changes to the check runner.
The prompt text states the reason for the rule, so an outside reader understands why docs-only changes still need the full test run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Today no code path re-invokes the producer: produce_and_verify in crates/athena-core/src/run.rs calls it once, and the candidate then goes straight to checks and verification. 'Sent back to the producer' therefore needs a small bounded retry in that function, which I assume the user wants.
The retry is limited to one extra producer invocation, to bound cost. If it is still not-run, the job fails with a clear reason and does not reach verification.

The gate keys on the producer's reported checks_run: an entry whose command is `cargo test --locked` with result not-run, or no such entry. Athena's own check runner is unchanged, though its skip_when_only patterns for docs and *.md remain; athena.toml line 79 already says the test check never skips.
The producer's Bash grant must allow `cargo test --locked`. athena.toml already lists cargo test as allowed, so no governance file changes. If the grant needs a change, that is a separate decision.
Only the shared producer frame (crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md) changes. The capability-specific producer.md files are left alone.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md no longer says the producer 'may' run the checks. It requires the producer to run the full `cargo test --locked` before finishing, for every change including docs, TOML and data-only ones. It names the reason: policy and config tests read tracked non-Rust files (boundary words, unlisted file kinds, defaults.toml, study model.json).
The prompt says a `not-run` full test result is not an acceptable finish, and that the producer must report the real result in checks_run.

A candidate whose producer report lists the full `cargo test --locked` as `not-run` (or lists no such check) is not sent to the verifier. The producer is re-invoked with a message explaining why, and a bounded retry count applies. Run `cargo test` and check that the new test for this gate passes.
A candidate whose report shows the full test run as pass or fail continues to verification as before. Run `cargo test` and check that the existing lifecycle and run tests still pass.
`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean, and prompt budget tests (crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs) still pass with the longer prompt.
Docs that describe the producer's checks (docs/design/athena-v0.md) match the new rule and the send-back behavior. The CHANGELOG records the change.

out_of_scope: Changing Athena's own check runner or the skip_when_only patterns in athena.toml
Changing the verifier or reader prompts
Changing the study capability's producer prompt
Making the producer run clippy or fmt as a hard requirement
departures: The request needs a prompt edit and a new retry path in produce_and_verify, which has no retry today. That makes the job larger than a typical prompt-only change, so I raised cost and time above the reference and lowered the pass probability.
